evidence.intree_statement: Class StrictMonoidal : Type := { strict_is_monoidal : @Monoidal C; strict_assoc_obj : forall X Y Z, ((X ⨂ Y) ⨂ Z) = (X ⨂ (Y ⨂ Z)); strict_unit_left_obj : forall X, (I ⨂ X) = X; strict_unit_right_obj : forall X, (X ⨂ I) = X; strict_assoc_to : to tensor_assoc ≈ match strict_assoc_obj … with eq_refl => id end; strict_unit_left_to : to unit_left ≈ … id; strict_unit_right_to : to unit_right ≈ … id }

statement_record.book: A monoidal category is strict when its structure isomorphisms — the associator α and the unitors λ, ρ — are all identities; equivalently the tensor is strictly associative and e is a strict two-sided unit (recalled from VII.1).
statement_record.intree: Class StrictMonoidal over a Monoidal C: the object-level Leibniz equalities (X⨂Y)⨂Z = X⨂(Y⨂Z), I⨂X = X, X⨂I = X, together with fields forcing to(tensor_assoc), to(unit_left), to(unit_right) to equal the identity transported along those equalities (with the from-directions derived as corollaries strict_*_from).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same (faithful setoid rendering). Because obj is a Type not a setoid, 'α,λ,ρ are identities' is rendered as BOTH object-level propositional equalities AND the structural isos equalling the transported id; the file's header explains this is the honest strict notion in a setoid library. If anything intree-stronger only in bookkeeping (it names the object equalities explicitly), not in mathematical content.

verifier.notes: Blind search independently found Structure/Monoidal/Strict.v as the sole strict-monoidal class. Read the file: Class StrictMonoidal begins at line 52, fields span 52-94, and the quoted intree_statement matches the code (object-level Leibniz equalities + strict_*_to forcing the structural isos to the transported id). File is registered in _CoqProject. The setoid rendering (object equalities plus transported-identity isos) is the faithful strict notion; strength 'same' is honest. Header (Strict.v:20-46) is accurate and matches the code.

aliases: all diagrams built from alpha commute

statement_record.book: If M is equivalent via a strong monoidal functor to a strict monoidal category S, then coherence for associativity (and for the unit isos ρ, λ) holds in M: any two natural transformations built from α (resp. ρ, λ) between the same pair of tensor-word functors are equal. Proof transports parallel canonical maps through the equivalence, where strictness of S collapses them to equality.
statement_record.intree: NO in-tree counterpart to the universal coherence theorem. There is no datatype of canonical/formal maps, no tensor-word functors, and no universally-quantified 'any two parallel canonical maps are equal' statement. The only related content is a fixed finite family of derived coherence corollaries in Structure/Monoidal/Proofs.v (triangle_identity_left:184, inverse_triangle_identity:201, inverse_pentagon_identity:215, triangle_identity_right:299, bimap_triangle_right:314, bimap_triangle_left:327, unit_identity/λ_I≈ρ_I:344) — Kelly's lemmas, proved directly from the pentagon/triangle AXIOMS. The file header (Proofs.v:14-20) itself frames these as consequences 'that Mac Lane's coherence theorem guarantees', treating the theorem as an EXTERNAL fact it does not formalize.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker to the point of absence: the theorem's distinctive content (the universal quantification over all canonical maps, obtained via strictification) has no in-tree carrier; only individual named low-arity diagrams (all direct axiom-consequences) are proved.

negative_search_log: grep -rn -i 'canonical map|all diagrams commute|coherence theorem|any two natural|word.*equal|two.*canonical|parallel.*canonical' — every hit tying 'coherence theorem' to monoidal categories is a header/essay reference (Structure/Monoidal.v:43,53,71; Structure/Monoidal/Proofs.v:16; Symmetric.v:47; Heunen_Vicary.v:58), not a theorem statement. The free-PROP universal property (Construction/PROP/Universal.v) is a coherence-type result but for STRICT SYMMETRIC monoidal targets over a signature — a different item, not the plain-monoidal associativity coherence of XI.3:thm2.

The only proven field literally named *coherence* is prop_monoidal_coherence (Construction/PROP.v:111) / cprop_monoidal_coherence — an eq_refl-computing OBJECT-LEVEL strictness equality of the strict symmetric PROP, NOT Mac Lane's associativity coherence theorem.

RELATED-BUT-NOT-THE-ITEM: Structure/Monoidal/Proofs.v proves Kelly's derived lemmas (triangle_identity_left:184 ... unit_identity/λ_I≈ρ_I:344), all direct corollaries of the pentagon+triangle axioms, standing alone; they instantiate no universal coherence statement and use no strictification. The via-strictification proof route the book uses is absent because strictification itself (XI.3:thm1) is ABSENT.

verifier.notes: Phase C classified PARTIAL on the strength of the Kelly's-lemmas evidence. I verified those lemmas DO exist at the cited lines (Proofs.v:184,201,215,299,314,327,344) and are honestly described — but they do not constitute partial coverage of THIS item. The item is the universal coherence THEOREM (any two parallel canonical maps between tensor-word functors are equal), obtained via strictification. In-tree: (1) there is NO notion of canonical map or tensor-word functor — zero infrastructure toward the theorem; (2) no universally-quantified coherence statement is proved; (3) the strictification route is absent (thm1 ABSENT, agreed by Phase C); (4) the proved lemmas are derived corollaries of the pentagon/triangle AXIOMS, and the file's own header (14-20) treats Mac Lane's coherence theorem as an EXTERNAL fact that 'guarantees' them 'without making them part of the data'. Proving a fixed finite set of named low-arity diagrams is the special-case-only pattern the adversarial pass targets, not a fragment of a metatheorem that has no in-tree carrier. Contrast with XI.3:ex1 (CONFIRMED PARTIAL), where the item's carrier object (the monoidal endofunctor category) genuinely exists and only a property is missing — here the theorem has no carrier at all. Downgraded to ABSENT; the Kelly lemmas are retained in the negative log as related-not-the-item so Phase E frames the issue as 'formalize the monoidal coherence theorem', not 'extend a partial one'.

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Compose_Monoidal {C : Category} : @Monoidal ([C, C]) := {| tensor := {| fobj := fun p => fst p ◯ snd p ; fmap := … Godement composite … |}; I := Id |}. (tensor = functor composition ◯, unit = identity functor Id.)
Theorem Monoid_Monad : @MonoidObject (Endofunctors C) Compose_Monoidal M ↔ Monad M.  (uses Compose_Monoidal as the monoidal structure on Endofunctors C := [C,C])

statement_record.book: For any category C the endofunctor category C^C, with composition of endofunctors as tensor and the identity functor 1_C as unit, is a strict monoidal category.
statement_record.intree: Compose_Monoidal : @Monoidal ([C, C]) gives the endofunctor category the monoidal structure with ◯ as tensor and Id as unit; its unitors and associator are component-wise identity natural isomorphisms. The header (Structure/Monoidal/Compose.v:35-40) explicitly states 'In the literature this monoidal structure is strict … Here it is nonetheless presented as a general (non-strict) Monoidal instance'.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the endofunctor category is given the monoidal structure of the exercise (composition tensor, Id unit) and it is genuinely used (Monad/Monoid.v), but it is registered only as a general @Monoidal, NOT as a @StrictMonoidal. The 'strict' upgrade — the point of the exercise — is deliberately not asserted; no StrictMonoidal instance for Compose_Monoidal exists in-tree (StrictMonoidal is instantiated only for PROPs).
